statements.attributed: HEAs form when the TΔS mix term drives the system
statements.quote: Thus, HEAs form when the TΔS mix term drives the system. High entropy intermetallics (HEIs) are related to HEAs but exhibit extended‐range chemical ordering through the emergence of sublattices, but with random mixing within at least one sublattice. The crystal structures of HEI NPs resemble that of their binary intermetallic counterparts, where metals with similar properties (e.g., atomic radius and electronegativity) occupy distinct sublattices, leading to a negative ΔH mix.

statements.attributed: PE core‐shell NPs with five elements can be annealed into HEA NPs
statements.cited_system: PE core‐shell NPs with five elements
statements.quote: In fact, we showed that PE core‐shell NPs with five elements can be annealed into HEA NPs. In contrast to direct colloidal synthesis of HEAs, this approach requires fewer metal precursors at each step, enabling the formation of monodisperse HEA samples with significantly greater synthetic control. However, this NP conversion method has not been shown to synthesize every type of PE NP and the general applicability of the process, grounded in thermodynamic principles, has not been presented previously.

statements.attributed: The synthesis of equimolar core‐shell NPs and their thermal conversion to HEA NPs was reported
statements.quote: Previously, we reported the synthesis of equimolar core‐shell NPs and their thermal conversion to HEA NPs. Thus, we hypothesized that precursor PE core‐shell NPs with nonequimolar stoichiometries could be prepared and serve as precursors to multiphase PE NPs (Figure 1).

statements.attributed: Standard methods were used to prepare Au2Cu and AuCu2 seeds
statements.quote: Specifically, Au2Cu and AuCu2 seeds (Figures S1, S2) were prepared by standard methods, followed by core‐shell NP syntheses where PtPdNi shells were deposited by coreduction of PtBr2, PdBr2, and Ni(acac)2 in a heated solution.

statements.attributed: Metals with stronger bonds tend to segregate together, while those with weaker bonds are more likely to alloy
statements.quote: By examining the bond dissociation energies for all possible metal pair combinations, we can predict that metals with stronger bonds will tend to segregate together, while those with weaker bonds are more likely to alloy. Figures 3 and S15–S26 show the atomistic simulations where we varied starting core‐shell stoichiometry (ideal equimolar ‐ AuCu@PtPdM ‐ to nonequimolar cores ‐ Au3Cu@PtPdM and AuCu3@PtPdM, where M is Ni or Fe), core‐shell NP size (8–14 nm), and match stoichiometries from experiments considering colloidal synthesis limitations (Table S1).

statements.attributed: Ni‐based NPs show a stronger tendency toward Janus‐like configurations compared to the Fe‐based NPs
statements.quote: The Ni‐based NPs show a stronger tendency toward Janus‐like configurations compared to the Fe‐based NPs (Figure 3e,f).

statements.attributed: A structure's anisotropy (lower packing fraction along the <h00> direction compared to <hhh>) is a key driver to elemental segregation
statements.quote: Simulations suggest a structure's anisotropy (i.e., lower packing fraction along the <h00> direction compared to <hhh>) is another key driver to elemental segregation (Figure S19). Directional preferential segregation is observed in the STEM‐EDS simulations for the Au3Cu core‐based and Fe‐based NPs (Figure 3e,f).

statements.attributed: Au has been shown to promote mixing and lower the disorder‐to‐order phase transition temperature (TPT d→o) in PtFe, thus enabling intermetallic formation at lower temperatures
statements.quote: Recently, Au has been shown to promote mixing and lower the disorder‐to‐order phase transition temperature (TPT d→o) in PtFe, thus enabling intermetallic formation at lower temperatures. Based on these observations, we hypothesized that equimolar NPs with AuCu cores and Pt, Fe, and Pd shells could result in HEI NPs upon annealing.

statements.attributed: Equimolar AuCu alloy NPs (size 8.2 ± 0.9 nm) were synthesized
statements.quote: First, equimolar AuCu alloy NPs (size 8.2 ± 0.9 nm) were synthesized (Figure S28). Then, these NPs were used as seeds to synthesize core‐shell AuCu@PtPdFe NPs, where PtPdFe shells were deposited by coreduction of PtBr2, PdBr2, and Fe(acac)3 in heated solution (Figure S29).

statements.attributed: Intermetallic compounds form more readily below the TPT d→o and an annealing temperature near or above TPT d→o hinders the disorder‐to‐order transition
statements.quote: Binary alloy phase diagrams indicate that intermetallic compounds form more readily below the TPT d→o and an annealing temperature near or above TPT d→o hinders the disorder‐to‐order transition. Therefore, an annealing temperature of ∼800 °C for the equimolar precursor core‐shell NP favors the formation of disordered or random alloy to ordered intermetallic either L10 fct‐PtFe or L12‐Pt3Fe phases (Pt‐Fe system TPT d→o ∼1300 °C) but theoretically should be unfavorable for intermetallic L10 fct or L12 PtxNi1‐x phases (Pt‐Ni system TPT d→o ∼630 °C) (Figure S32).

statements.attributed: Intraparticle heterogeneity is challenging to detect experimentally
statements.quote: We note that, although intraparticle heterogeneity—previously discussed in our earlier work—is challenging to detect experimentally, both our current experimental data and simulations provide no evidence for its presence in this study. Surface relaxation‐induced segregation likely prevents our simulations from unequivocally supporting the formation of HEI or HEA NPs from equimolar core‐shell PE NPs.
